source.title: Belfast Newsletter, 8 June 1964, p. 9 ("Hillsborough Rural District Council: notice of result of elections, 1964"); Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1964, p. 2 ("Hillsborough Labour man polls 17 votes")
source.publisher: Belfast Newsletter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: names and votes read on the page images of the notice (8 June 1964, p. 9) and the results paragraph (5 June 1964, p. 2): Johnston 291, White (Lab.) 148, Kingan 107 (council-audit, Nov 2026).

note: Triennial election of Hillsborough Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Hillsborough, Maze and Anahilt were contested and the other thirteen divisions were returned unopposed. Three candidates; the notice prints no party labels, the News-Letter's report of 5 June 1964 (p. 2) labels George White Labour and gives a 90.81 per cent poll. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026).
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of the Belfast News-Letter, 8 June 1964, p. 9 and 5 June 1964, p. 2 (council-audit, Nov 2026): William Thompson Crossey (204) stood in Maze, not Hillsborough, and is moved to the Maze contest; the majority of 87 (computed against Crossey) is removed (against White it would be 143, not printed); George White's Labour label and the 90.81 per cent poll added from the 5 June report.
